videos.script: So far every vector in this course came from a model running on your own machine. Most teams get theirs from an API instead. {{api}} You send text over HTTP, and a provider sends numbers back. This lesson uses the real OpenAI Python library to do that. {{sdk}} The server it talks to is the lab's own stand-in, called labembed. It speaks OpenAI's format, so the code is the code you would ship. Only the address and the model name change. {{labembed}} You will read a response field by field, and catch the library quietly asking for base64 instead of numbers. {{wire}} You will send the whole help centre in batches, and count its tokens the way the bill does. {{batch}} You will ask for shorter vectors and measure what they cost in search quality. {{dimensions}} You will price a million documents from a published sheet. {{cost}} And you will watch the library retry a rate limit by itself, and then give up. {{retry}} By the end, an embeddings API is one more function you know how to call, and how to pay for. {{end}}
